summary: Thubten Chodron works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan and Dorje Pamo monasteries, and under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama. She later served at Dharma Friendship Foundation and founded Sravasti Abbey, serving as abbess.

Thubten Chökyi Dorje (1872–1935) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Patrul Rinpoche, and taught disciples including Chatral Sangye Dorje, Shenphen Nangwa, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Thubten Jigme Norbu (1922–2008) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992).
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. As a teacher, his students included Thubten Jigme Norbu, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa, and the 14th Dalai Lama.

Thubten Samphel (1956–2022) was a Tibetology scholar who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi (~1974–1979), and Columbia University (~1980–1981). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, Zongkar Choede Monastery, and the University of Cambridge. He taught at Ganden, founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics, and was a research fellow at Girton College.

Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was an Indology and Sinology scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew lessons and lectures at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Thích Minh Châu (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University, lectured in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1952–1961), and served as Vice Chancellor of Van Hanh University (~1964–1975).

Thích Thiện Châu (1931–1998) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He pursued his education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and completing his doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1971–1977).

Tianshu Zhu works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at Northwest University and a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She has held posts at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Korea University, and Ohio State.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, earning his PhD at the University of Vienna. He succeeded David Seyfort Ruegg and was a professor at Leiden University (~1976–2002).
Timothy Asch (1932–1994) was educated at The Putney School (~1947–1951), Columbia University (~1955–1959), Boston University, and Harvard University.

Timothy H. Barrett is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Cambridge and Yale University. He taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) and was appointed Professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy J. Dean studied under Robert Clark, earning a BA from the University of East Anglia, and studied at Brandeis University and Johns Hopkins University (PhD). He held a fellowship at Stanford University (1997–1998) and a post at UIUC.

Timothy Lenz specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, and later held positions at the University of Washington, including faculty and professor (attested 1998–2026).
Timothy Lubin is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1994. He has held an academic post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, the University of Mysore, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari and others. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1953).

Tiruvengadu Narayanayajwa Ramachandran (1901–1973) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (attested 1933) and later as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

Tissa Rajapatirana is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong and later held a post there in the Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).
